headline: Cybersecurity Software Surges as Financials Lead a Broad Wednesday Advance
body_html:
Wednesday's session, November 18, closed with buyers firmly in control: 417 stocks rose and 244 fell across our 664-name universe. The dominant theme was a surge in cybersecurity software. Tenable led the board with a 15.75% jump, followed by Qualys at 12.92%, Netskope at 12.73% and Okta at 12.07%. Edge-cloud name Fastly added 12.58%.

The rotation reached well beyond tech. Financials were the best sector, up 3.18%, and consumer shares gained 2.39%. Software rose 1.49% and homebuilders 1.48%, with industrials up 0.9%. Materials edged up 0.21%, semiconductors were flat at -0.04%, healthcare slipped 0.33% and energy dropped 1.82%. Minutes showing Fed officials expect further rate increases formed the backdrop, though no single headline fully explains the move.

The rally was selective. BlackLine fell 8.08% even as its software peers climbed, and gold miners DRDGOLD and Agnico Eagle lost 6.99% and 6.43%. A market can rise this broadly and still punish individual stories sharply. Thursday will show whether the enthusiasm for security software carries over or fades.

briefs.headline: Fed Minutes Point to Further Tightening
briefs.body: Minutes from the latest Fed meeting show officials expect additional rate increases. Some are also concerned that artificial intelligence could add to inflation pressure. Financials still led Wednesday's session, rising 3.18% as the sector's gains outran the rate worries.

briefs.headline: Energy Slides Despite Iran Tensions
briefs.body: Washington tightened its Iran blockade with new limits on at-sea oil transfers, and US intelligence officials say threats from Tehran have grown. Even so, energy was the weakest sector, down 1.82%. Baytex Energy fell 6.31%, among the day's heavier declines.

briefs.headline: Gold Miners Hit as Metals Tumble
briefs.body: Metals sold off ahead of a heavily anticipated AI listing, and gold producers took the brunt of it. DRDGOLD dropped 6.99% and Agnico Eagle lost 6.43%. Materials as a whole still managed a small 0.21% gain, held up by other corners of the group.

briefs.headline: Housing Starts Rebound, but Slowly
briefs.body: Single-family housing starts recovered, though the broader trend remains subdued. Investors still gave homebuilders a warm reception, and the group gained 1.48% on the session, trailing only financials, consumer and software.

briefs.headline: Sellers Appear Ahead of Anthropic's Debut
briefs.body: Commentary on the coming Anthropic IPO says the intense interest is also drawing sellers, who see the down market as offering a silver lining. Optical-components maker Applied Optoelectronics fell 9.8%, the worst move among our decliners, while semiconductors finished flat.

briefs.headline: Vital Farms Joins the Consumer Charge
briefs.body: Vital Farms jumped 13.61%, the second-biggest gain in our universe and a standout in a consumer group that rose 2.39%. The rally came in a session where gainers outnumbered decliners by roughly five to three, 417 to 244.
